title: I need help with more complex logic.
author: Same_Opposite6306
selftext:
I’ve been trying to build a terrain LOD streaming system for some time. Ultimately, it’s a quad-sphere subdivided via a quadtree. I tried doing it myself for months before eventually turning to "agentic coding."   
However, my attempts are failing here as well. The problem is that quadtree leaves are sometimes created on-demand with a delay, since the terrain is generated procedurally and asynchronously using Burst. The agents seem to struggle significantly with time-dependent states.   
Do you have any ideas or approaches for effectively designing or implementing such complex systems using agents?

comments.author: 3tt07kjt
comments.body:
This is where you bust out Fable to plan things out. 

Look for concurrent / parallel design patterns that simplify one or more aspects of it, like serializing mutations through one thread, and using immutable data. Unfortunately this is a classic systems design type problem so there is no simple thing I can say that explains all you need to know. But Fable is a good baseline for this.

replies.author: Same_Opposite6306
replies.body: I’ve been using Astra in Fable as an "architecture challenger" to plan and optimize everything—for instance, pitting Morton codes against Hilbert curves. I just get the feeling I’m doing something fundamentally wrong. I plan the implementation in detail across multiple iterations, instruct an orchestrator agent to execute it and delegate tasks to sub-agents, and—due to usage limits—have it built over the course of several days, yet it keeps failing.

replies.author: 3tt07kjt
replies.body: How much programming experience do you have? Have you implemented any parallel algorithms before (something more than map/reduce)?

replies.author: Same_Opposite6306
replies.body: I work in the IT sector. While I’m no longer an application developer, I have previously developed WebGL and mobile apps. I’ve dealt with asynchronous processing and server-client communication (including latency issues) before, but not at this level of complexity; most of the applications I worked on were primarily frontend-focused. I understand the fundamental problem. The meshes are being generated correctly, and leaf addressing works fine. My specific challenge is developing a system that is both performant—meaning decoupled from rendering and the like—and reliable (deterministic). I need to swap leaves with lower LOD for those with higher LOD without creating holes in the terrain, even if the leaf generation takes a few milliseconds longer.

replies.author: 3tt07kjt
replies.body:
There’s a noticeable step in difficulty when working with parallel programming, as opposed to asynchronous code with clear boundaries (like a typical client / server setup). Might be worth spending some time studying / practicing this. Maybe some of it with limited AI use (not zero, just limited). It sounds like you have the right background to study this. I would ask the AI for a book recommendation for parallel programming.

There are also likely some articles in e.g. Graphics Gems that cover terrain systems, or papers you can read that cover exactly what you’re doing.
